concepts.title: 5.6 Sol — Index House
concepts.design_contract_summary: A stable destination directory loads one category into a three-pane workspace with a nested directory, continuous document, and value-source/effect inspector.

impacts.requirement: Represent the packet's humanized category and subcategory hierarchy as stable addresses without primary category pills.
impacts.selected_concept_behavior: Numbered destination rows open one category; nested directory entries and semantic subcategory anchors preserve location.
supersedes_or_conflicts_with: PMConcept7 primary category pill behavior in this redesign lane
Current settings inventory mixes user goals and internal implementation boundaries
wiring_routes: Settings Home search result -> owner category -> semantic subcategory anchor -> setting focus
Directory category selection -> one-category document model
Intersection-observed chapter -> scrollspy state
schema_or_event_impacts: Canonical category aliases may need stable migration fields
Setting source, scope, exposure, requested value, and effective value need typed presentation state
demo_fixture_impacts: Ten category fixtures, twenty subcategories, and seventy-two data-backed settings
Default, Inherited, Auto, Not configured, Managed, Custom, Unavailable, Effective value differs, independent recommendation marks, and all six exposure levels
test_impacts: Stable deep-link offset
Scrollspy does not oscillate
Squeezed directory becomes a navigator without clipping
slint_notes: Use a ListModel for categories and section models for settings
Translate IntersectionObserver to viewport section-position signals without making geometry product state
notes: Concept fixture IDs are not canonical settings IDs.
No inventory or Plans content was changed.

impacts.requirement: Open dedicated managers from both category context and the Home specialist-room directory.
impacts.selected_concept_behavior: The inspector routes to the related manager while the Home directory exposes all ten manager families.
wiring_routes: Category inspector -> related manager overview
Manager Home action -> Settings Home
Restore category defaults -> confirmation/receipt path
schema_or_event_impacts: Manager navigation history should retain the originating setting or category
test_impacts: Back navigation and focus restoration
Every manager action mutates state or returns an honest receipt
slint_notes: Manager shells can share state/actions while each concept supplies an adapter layout
notes: Candidate command names are descriptive only and were not minted.

concepts.title: 5.6 Sol — Switchboard
concepts.design_contract_summary: An operational board organizes Settings around readiness, health, explicit actions, station switching, a vertical signal track, and an effective-state tray.

impacts.requirement: Expose readiness, loading, refreshing, degraded, setup, unavailable, managed, and last-known-good state without reducing Settings to alerts.
impacts.selected_concept_behavior: Home readouts and destination bays summarize readiness; the workspace tray explains effective state and future/in-flight boundaries.
supersedes_or_conflicts_with: Horizontal notice rail behavior from PMConcept7 is replaced for this redesign concept
Detailed usage remains owned by Usage even when Settings shows a snapshot
wiring_routes: Provider/Usage health snapshot -> Settings status readout
Readiness signal action -> owning manager detail
Requested state + live capacity/policy -> effective-state explanation
schema_or_event_impacts: Readiness evidence needs source, observed-at, freshness, last-known-good, and quarantine fields
Requested/effective state needs reason and owner provenance
demo_fixture_impacts: Normal, Needs attention, Calm, Setup in progress, Loading, Refreshing, Degraded with last-known-good data, Managed workspace, Unavailable dependency, Error, Usage exhausted, and Requested/effective difference scenarios
Provider refresh retains catalogue rows while validation runs
test_impacts: No permanent pulse in calm state
Refresh failure preserves last-known-good rows
Status actions resolve to owner surfaces
slint_notes: Readiness should be a normalized Rust state model, not inferred from visual style
Station and signal transitions require transform/opacity equivalents
notes: Settings usage snapshots must not duplicate the full Usage concept.

impacts.requirement: Represent provider family, account/profile, connection, product/plan, model evidence, and role assignment as separate operational levels.
impacts.selected_concept_behavior: A topology-like provider board exposes isolated accounts, future-only selection, in-flight capture, refresh, model gates, and support receipts.
supersedes_or_conflicts_with: Generic account switching that does not preserve an in-flight route
Treating CLI-owned OAuth as Puppet Master direct OAuth
wiring_routes: Provider refresh -> discovery -> validation -> last-known-good commit or quarantine
Future account choice -> new-request route preference without mutating captured in-flight work
Free route setup -> underlying provider/account/model owner
schema_or_event_impacts: Account profile isolation and authentication owner need explicit fields
Fast and effort support need evidence-qualified capability records
Usage exhaustion needs provider-specific next-action state
demo_fixture_impacts: Same-provider multi-account, API, CLI-owned OAuth, server, signed-out, not-installed, failed invocation, free setup, keyless, and exhausted-usage fixtures
test_impacts: Unsupported Fast/effort controls remain absent
Authentication success does not imply generation readiness
Account selection is future-only
slint_notes: Provider and model lists should be virtualized ListModels
Refresh must update the model atomically after validation
notes: Provider names and capability timestamps are fixtures, not current provider truth.

concepts.title: 5.6 Sol — Wayfinder
concepts.design_contract_summary: A human-goal taxonomy turns Settings categories into routes and subcategories into checkpoints while preserving canonical area names and expert branches.

impacts.requirement: Search and navigation must support human outcomes without hiding canonical category ownership.
impacts.selected_concept_behavior: Routes pair an outcome label with the owning category; search returns both the target and its humanized route.
supersedes_or_conflicts_with: Current inventory labels that expose internal subsystem boundaries as the only navigation language
wiring_routes: Humanized search token -> canonical owner category alias -> subcategory/setting deep link
Journey map selection -> category replacement
Checkpoint selection -> semantic anchor and controlled scroll
schema_or_event_impacts: Canonical categories may need localized search aliases and outcome descriptions
Aliases must migrate independently from stable setting identity
demo_fixture_impacts: Outcome aliases for all required packet domains
test_impacts: Search by outcome lands on the canonical owner
Canonical and humanized names remain visible together
Checkpoint scrollspy remains stable
slint_notes: Route lines are decorative; semantic state remains a route/category model
Narrow navigator becomes a full-height stateful overlay
notes: Route aliases are concept proposals and were not added to canonical inventory.

impacts.requirement: Provider, Memory, and Terminal managers may use guided setup/inspect/repair steps without hiding expert state.

wiring_routes: Manager problem state -> bounded setup/inspect/repair step -> receipt

test_impacts: Expert state remains reachable

slint_notes: Use explicit manager-step state rather than relying on CSS expansion
notes: No production wizard lifecycle is implied by this concept.

concepts.title: 5.6 Sol — Ledger
concepts.design_contract_summary: A dense reference register and continuous folio prioritize comparison, requested/effective values, source, scope, history, and manager evidence.

impacts.requirement: Make default, inherited, managed, unavailable, requested, and effective values comparable without exposing raw internal enums.
impacts.selected_concept_behavior: Rows and manager facts expose humanized status plus source/scope; explicit comparison cells distinguish requested from effective state.
supersedes_or_conflicts_with: Any single-value presentation that hides policy, qualification, or capacity substitution
wiring_routes: Stored request + policy/qualification/capacity state -> effective value + reason + owner
Reset action -> owning default/inheritance resolver -> receipt
schema_or_event_impacts: Effective-value derivation needs reason, owner, observed-at, and source revision
Reset must distinguish default restoration from inheritance restoration
Managed and unavailable states need user-readable reasons
demo_fixture_impacts: Managed organization policy and unavailable language-support examples
test_impacts: Requested and effective values never collapse into one ambiguous field
Reset/inherit/default labels remain distinct
No raw enum or identifier appears in ordinary UI
slint_notes: Comparison rows should receive derived display state from Rust
Dense table columns need explicit breakpoint layouts
notes: Canonical storage/event shapes were not inferred or edited.

impacts.requirement: Support a dense destination register and long manager inventories without unbounded DOM-style rendering.

wiring_routes: Register row -> category folio
Minimap row -> semantic chapter jump
Manager ledger row -> evidence detail

demo_fixture_impacts: Long-list fixtures should be expanded for native virtualization profiling
test_impacts: Keyboard traversal of virtual rows
Squeezed hierarchy tables reflow into labelled entries without page-level horizontal scroll

cross_concept_findings.finding: The current settings inventory mixes human goals and internal subsystem boundaries; all four concepts preserve complete domain discoverability while proposing different humanized presentation layers.

Search, category replacement, semantic anchors, scrollspy, setting rows, receipts, provider state, Memory evidence, and Terminal profiles can share normalized state without forcing a shared visual adapter.

Settings should display source-labelled provider usage summaries and provider-specific next actions while handing off exact provider/account context to the Usage owner for detailed history and analysis; the concept-local handoff remains an explicit simulation receipt.
Spellcheck behavior needs command and storage adjudication for source selection, personal/project dictionary scope, exclusion rules, replace-once, ignore, and dictionary actions.
No candidate command in this register is minted. Existing command identity, payload, permission, receipt, and undo semantics require canonical lookup and owner adjudication before promotion.
Provider capability and freshness labels in this bakeoff are deterministic fixtures and must not be promoted as current provider evidence.

Production demo and test fixtures need one normalized graph for settings provenance; provider families, accounts, connections, products, routes, adapters and evidence; eleven role assignments; Memory versions; Terminal drafts; spelling exclusions; domain-specific Context, Persona, Crew, MCP, LSP, extension/tool and Media inventories; scenario overlays; setup sessions; recent changes; and persistent receipts.

Navigation, category replacement, search, jump, scrollspy, disclosure, refresh, save, reorder, and drawer motion should share semantic transaction keys while each selected presentation owns its choreography; participant roles and keyed entity targets need testable bindings, and native Slint should map the same keys to cancelable property animations and temporary proxy components.

Production responsive and accessibility contracts need explicit effective-main-width breakpoints, reachable pane-to-drawer-to-inline adaptations, narrow list/detail focus restoration, semantic combobox/tab/menu/drawer primitives, inert hidden panels, forced-colors tokens, RTL direction handling, text expansion, coarse-pointer targets, and reduced-motion parity.
